thread:
taylor: Heads-up — I started a long-run fuzz job on the paging branch and saw steady VRAM growth until OOM on H100 cluster after ~45m. Not the usual reclaim pattern.
alex_g: Can you paste the run config and kernel logs? sounds like an evict path isn't honoring a threshold.
taylor: repro command: `./run_longctx_test --model=gpt-3-like --seq=131072 --batch=4 --gpu=h100-8 --kvcache=pagetable-async-evict`\nlog snippet:\n```
[2026-02-14T18:22:31Z] kvcache: allocate page slot=0x1f2a, owner=worker-7
[2026-02-14T18:22:31Z] pagetable: mark-rot threshold=4096, idx=4095 -> rotate
[2026-02-14T18:22:33Z] async-evict: queued page 0x1f2a for eviction on device 1
[2026-02-14T18:22:33Z] async-evict: completed page 0x1f2a -> freed on device 0 (unexpected)
```
alex_g: oh that's odd — eviction completed on device 0 while queued for device 1. NVLink topology mismatch maybe? any cross-device copies happening?
maria_r: linking to the kernel trace I grabbed: `perf trace -p 2345` shows `memcpyPeer` on the path but no fence before free. might be a missing cudaEvent/sync in the async-evict completion.
jamal: Could be a race between rotate increment and the page owner being reparented. If rotate threshold is computed per-host-page but evict works per-device, we can free a page while another device still references it.
taylor: Agree. I also saw the pagetable rotate counter wrap when seq > 2^12 in our profiling run, which causes eviction heuristics to think the slot is 'cold' again. That's why it kept getting reallocated and leaked metadata.
perf-bot: perf-summary: longctx_run_6520099999 -> token/s drop 18%, 6% sys mem growth per 10k tokens, top flame: kvcache::evict_worker -> cudaMemcpyPeer -> host_free
alex_g: Repro steps I used on my workstation (smaller): `python -m infra.repro --seed=42 --len=200k --gpu=1 --kvcache-page-size=64KB --rotate-threshold=4096` produced same pattern but slower. Attaching minimal trace and a tiny patch I used to assert device-id on free.
taylor: Patch I think we need: ensure async-evict completion callback records device id and delays host-free until all peer fences observed. Also fix rotate counter to use 64-bit monotonic counter to avoid wrap on long contexts.
maria_r: Small code snippet I proposed to test quickly:\n```
// in async evict cb
if (page->device_id != cb_device) {
  log("mismatched-device-free", page->id, page->device_id, cb_device);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize(cb_device); // temp assert
}
host_free(page->meta);
```
jamal: That sync will slow perf but is a good assert. If it repros consistently we can replace with cudaEvent/fence and proper cross-device signaling.
alex_g: I ran with the assert and the run failed fast with an explicit mismatch (device 1 vs cb 0). Repro binary: `build/repro/kvcache_async_evict_assert --iters=1000`.
taylor: Plan: (1) add assertion guard in main branch, (2) implement event-fence-based release in next PR, (3) increase rotate counter width, (4) add a regression test that runs longctx sampling for 1h on small infra. Anyone object?
maria_r: +1. I'll own the test harness for the regression and add an alert if metadata growth rate > 1% per 10k tokens.
jamal: I'll do the event fence impl, aiming for non-blocking release.
alex_g: I'll open the PRs and include perf numbers before/after.
deploy-bot: Deployed branch "kvcache-async-evict-assert" to staging at 2026-02-14T19:05:01Z :rocket:
taylor: Thanks all. leaving the long fuzz running — will post updates if growth stops or if new anomalies appear. :thumbsup:
